title: WCAG Levels: A, AA, or AAA?

scenes.line1: Do all sites need AAA accessibility?
scenes.say: Do you really need the strictest accessibility level for every site? Let's break down what the WCAG levels actually mean.
WCAG has three levels. Level A covers the basics. Level AA is the recommended standard, balancing usability and effort. Level AAA is the strictest, but almost no site meets every AAA rule.
For example, AA requires a contrast ratio of four and a half to one for text. AAA bumps that up to seven to one, which is much harder to achieve.

scenes.question: Should you always aim for AAA?
scenes.right: No, AA is practical for most sites. Discuss AAA features with stakeholders if needed.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: aiming for AAA on every project. In reality, AA is the practical baseline. I talk through any AAA features with the team if they're needed.
